rationale: Interpreted the retained receipt of the first probe: the two bounded-recovery comparisons are violated with valid witnesses (parsed indices 5 and 11) while all four flag-disabled controls hold, but comparisons 1, 3 and 4, which compare the restarted instance's configuration with the configuration entry in its log, are unknown because the harness's restart_observation event omitted the config_entry_in_applied_prefix operand those comparisons use as an applicability condition; the same parsed events do carry latest_config_index, latest_config_voters, the server sets, log_config_index and last_applied and show the empty and snapshot-derived configurations. Added that operand to restart_observation, added a fifth within-flag case whose committed configuration entry stays above the replayed committed prefix to separate the skipped entry from the flag itself, and registered the changed harness as a successor execution. Also answered the repair gap partially from source, cited the receipt in the configuration-context knowledge, and restated the question's discriminator.

investigations.discriminator: Whether the configuration predicates (latest_config_index and the server set against the configuration entry in the node's own log) evaluate as violated now that restart_observation emits the applied-prefix operand, and whether the within-flag case whose configuration entry stays above the replayed committed prefix reconstructs the committed single-voter configuration and recovers leadership, which would exclude the flag's committed-log replay itself as the cause of the non-progress.

knowledge.statement: The configuration a node holds decides its own participation and support arithmetic: runFollower declines to campaign when latestIndex is zero or the local ID has no vote in the latest configuration, a candidate needs quorumSize() votes of the latest configuration, and the leader's commitment is constructed from the latest configuration, so a stale or empty reconstruction directly changes which support is required and counted.
knowledge.conditions: The configuration is the one reconstructed at startup or later written by a snapshot install or a configuration change; quorumSize and the commitment are computed from configurations.latest.

knowledge.statement: In the retained restart executions, when the tracked commit index covered the node's last configuration entry, the restarted instance's configuration was not the one recorded in its own log: in the no-snapshot shape it held no servers at all (latest_config_index 0, latest_config_voters 0) while its log held a single-voter configuration entry at index 1 and last_applied was 101, and in the snapshot-then-remove shape it held index 1 with the two voters carried by its own snapshot metadata while its log held the single-voter configuration entry committed at index 103 and last_applied was 111; the public GetConfiguration view reported the same stale or empty configuration, and the flag-disabled controls in the same shapes reported latest_config_index equal to the log configuration entry index (1 and 103) with matching server sets.
knowledge.conditions: NewRaft restart over the same log, stable and snapshot stores with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a commit-tracking log store; no other instance left running and no later membership change. Comparisons 1, 3 and 4 of receipt 7939a2d6d98b4b42a3f261cd1eadc53f are unknown because the applicability operand was not emitted, so these are parsed event operands rather than completed comparisons.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 7939a2d6d98b4b42a3f261cd1eadc53f (completed, exit 0, TestAssuranceRestoreCommittedLogsContext passed) contradicts the bounded-recovery predicate in both single-voter restart shapes with the flag enabled and holds it in all four flag-disabled controls. Comparison 6 (node_progress, no_snapshot, flag on) is violated with a valid witness at parsed index 5: the restarted instance that was the only member of the committed configuration never became leader in the 3000 ms window, stayed Follower, made zero election attempts (pre_vote_requests 0) and reported latest_config_index 0 with an empty server set, while its own log held a single-voter configuration entry at index 1 and last_applied was 101. Comparison 8 (node_progress, config_after_snapshot, flag on) is violated with a valid witness at parsed index 11: the restarted sole member of the committed single-voter configuration stayed Candidate with 37 pre-vote campaigns and no leader, holding latest_config_index 1 with the two voters of its own snapshot metadata, while its log held the single-voter configuration entry committed at index 103 and last_applied was 111. Comparisons 0, 2, 5 and 7 hold: with the flag disabled the same restarts reported latest_config_index equal to the log configuration entry index (1 and 103) with matching server sets and reached Leader promptly. The causal reading is the source-based one recorded in @scan_behavior, @restore_advance and @context_consumers: the flag advances lastApplied to the tracked commit index before NewRaft's configuration scan [restore_lastapplied, scan_start], the scan starts above that index so the committed configuration entry is never re-derived, and the resulting context is what runFollower, quorumSize and the commitment consume. Countervailing detail: comparisons 1, 3 and 4, which compare the reconstructed configuration against the configuration entry, are unknown in this receipt because restart_observation did not emit the config_entry_in_applied_prefix operand they filter on (diagnostics at parsed indices 4 and 10), so the reconstruction is currently supported by the parsed operands listed in @reconstruction_observed plus source rather than by a completed comparison; the successor execution registered in this update emits that operand and re-evaluates those predicates. The competing explanation that the flag's committed-log replay itself, rather than the skipped configuration entry, blocks recovery is not excluded by this receipt: the successor's fifth case keeps the flag enabled but leaves the committed configuration entry above the replayed prefix, and construction-time feedback there reconstructs the single-voter configuration and elects the instance. Beyond this receipt the exercised scope is single-process in-memory stores, and the safety direction in which the skipped entries add voters (a reconstructed quorum smaller than the committed one) remains source-supported but unexecuted.

2708fe4120de4b7b945ec449b641cfed-gap-0.explanation: Source: a follower re-derives its configuration only from entries an AppendEntries newly appends, so entries it already holds at the same index and term are skipped and a healthy leader's ordinary replication does not repair the reconstruction [append_new]; snapshots are shipped only when the leader cannot produce the follower's previous log entry, and a new client membership change appends a new configuration entry that does repair it [install_snapshot_cfg, cfg_entry]. The receipt's two failing shapes left no other instance running and issued no further membership change, so no repair path was reachable there; the live-cluster case with a healthy leader and matching logs is still unexecuted.

limitations: Comparisons 1, 3 and 4 are unknown in the retained receipt because restart_observation omitted the config_entry_in_applied_prefix operand; the successor execution emits it and decides those predicates.

The bounded progress observation is a 3000 ms window (60 x ElectionTimeout of 50 ms) in a single process with in-memory stores; it is not an unbounded liveness proof, and the probe cannot show that no later repair occurs.
Not exercised: disk-backed commit-tracking stores, crashes during the restart, multi-member committed configurations, and post-restart client membership changes or snapshot installs.

Source-supported but unexecuted: when the skipped committed entries add voters, the reconstructed configuration has fewer voters than the committed one, so quorumSize() and the leader commitment can treat support that is not a majority of the committed configuration as sufficient.
counterevidence: The feature's documented purpose is replaying known-committed logs into the FSM; nothing in the sources makes skipping committed configuration entries a required behaviour, and the existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs asserts only applied index, tracked commit index and log indices, so it neither exercises nor contradicts the configuration reconstruction.

Competing explanation for the two violated comparisons: the committed-log replay the flag enables, rather than the configuration entry left below the applied index, could itself delay or prevent leadership recovery. This receipt does not separate the two; the successor's within-flag case (configuration entry above the replayed prefix) is registered to decide it, and construction-time feedback there reconstructs the committed single-voter configuration and elects the instance, which points away from the flag itself.

experiment.revision_reason: The restart_observation event now emits the config_entry_in_applied_prefix operand (with last_applied and log_config_index) so the configuration-reconstruction comparisons can evaluate, and a fifth within-flag case was added in which the committed configuration entry stays above the replayed committed prefix (staged commit index 102 versus entry index 103), separating the skipped configuration entry from the flag's own committed-log replay as the cause of the observed non-progress.

scope.description: Restart reconstruction of a Raft node's own configuration: five in-process cases over the captured package's own test facilities. Two single-voter shapes (no snapshot; snapshot then a committed RemoveServer of the non-leader peer) are each run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled, and a fifth case repeats the snapshot-then-remove shape with the flag enabled but nothing dispatched after the removal, so the committed configuration entry stays above the commit index the restart replays. Each case applies 100 commands through the leader, reads the configuration entry, tracked commit index and snapshot metadata from the surviving instance's own stores, stops every instance, and restarts the surviving voter with NewRaft over the same stores and a fresh in-memory transport.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across the restart and no other instance is left running to send entries.

In every shape the committed configuration after setup is a single-voter configuration: the bootstrap configuration with no snapshot, or the configuration left by a committed RemoveServer that follows a snapshot, while the snapshot metadata still names two voters.
The bounded progress window is 3000 ms (60 x ElectionTimeout = 50 ms, HeartbeatTimeout = 50 ms), and every flag-enabled case is paired with a flag-disabled control or with the within-flag case.

The fifth case relies on the tracked commit index lagging the committed configuration entry when nothing is dispatched after the removal; the actual values are emitted as staged_commit_index and log_config_index in its restart_inputs event.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, process crashes during the restart, and post-restart client membership changes or snapshot installs that could rewrite the configuration.

parameters.post_remove_applies: 10 for the config_after_snapshot cases, 0 for config_above_replayed_prefix
parameters.cases: no_snapshot flag-off/flag-on, config_after_snapshot flag-off/flag-on, config_above_replayed_prefix flag-on

experiment.prefix: The single generated test builds each case with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 1 or 2, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), applies 100 commands through the elected leader, and for the snapshot shapes calls leader.Snapshot() followed by leader.RemoveServer(non-leader ID) and, when the case asks for it, a fixed number of further applies before a final VerifyLeader. Before the restart it reads, from the surviving instance's own stores, the last configuration-carrying log entry (index, decoded server list), the snapshot metadata's ConfigurationIndex and server list, and the commit-tracking store's staged commit index; it then shuts down every instance and restarts the survivor with NewRaft over the same stores and a fresh in-memory transport wrapped in a counter for RequestPreVote/RequestVote. Each emitted CA_EVENT JSON line carries scenario and restore_committed_logs as identity, the instance's own configuration and its public GetConfiguration view, latest_config_index, latest_config_voters, the server sets, log_config_index, snapshot_config_index, last_applied, staged_commit_index, the derived config_entry_in_applied_prefix (with both operands), election attempts and became_leader over the bounded window.
experiment.responsibility: NewRaft owns the reconstruction of a node's own configuration from its durable stores, and the reconstructed configurations.latest is the only input to the node's own election gating, quorumSize and leader commitment; no component outside Raft is required to repair it.

comparisons.description: Control for the no-snapshot shape: with restore committed logs disabled the restarted voter's latest configuration index should equal the index of the configuration entry persisted in its own log.

No-snapshot shape with restore committed logs enabled and the configuration entry inside the replayed committed prefix: the restarted instance's latest configuration index is compared with the configuration entry index in its own log.
Control for the snapshot-then-remove shape: with the flag disabled the restarted voter should pick up the configuration entry committed after the snapshot.

Snapshot-then-remove shape with the flag enabled: the configuration entry committed after the snapshot lies inside the replayed committed prefix, and the restarted instance's latest configuration index is compared with it.

Identifies the origin of the reconstructed value: whether the restarted instance's configuration server set equals the configuration carried by its own snapshot metadata rather than the configuration entry in its log.
Control: the restarted sole voter of the no-snapshot shape reaches Leader inside the bounded window when restore committed logs is disabled.
No-snapshot shape with the flag enabled: the restarted sole voter of the committed configuration reaches Leader inside the bounded window.
Control: the restarted sole voter of the snapshot-then-remove shape reaches Leader inside the bounded window when the flag is disabled.
Snapshot-then-remove shape with the flag enabled: the restarted sole voter of the committed single-voter configuration reaches Leader inside the bounded window.

Within-flag control: with the flag enabled but the committed configuration entry above the replayed committed prefix, the restarted instance's latest configuration index should still equal the configuration entry index in its own log.
Within-flag control for progress: with the flag enabled and the configuration entry above the replayed committed prefix, the restarted sole voter reaches Leader inside the bounded window.
